_comment: Template config for the sdlc plugin. Copy it into the driven repo as `sdlc-pipeline.config.json` (at the root, `.config/` or `.claude/`) and replace every value below; the plugin ships no real config. Despite the `projectFields` name, none of this is a GitHub Projects-v2 board field -- every id here is one of GitHub's ORG-LEVEL custom Issue Types/Issue Fields (the same family: Settings -> Issue types / Issue fields for your org), automatically available on every repo in the org once created, no Projects-v2 board required at all. Look every id up once via `gh api graphql` introspection. See README.md.
_requiredWorkflows_comment: Each entry mirrors one GHA workflow's `paths:` filter: `prefixes`/`files` its paths, `excludeGlobs` its negations (`!**/*.md`). Optional `commandPattern`: a regex the `record-local-ci --command` must match. `suite` keys: letters, digits, `_`, `-`.

projectFields._issueTypeIds_comment: Mandatory: create-issue sets a native Issue Type on every issue it files and refuses a type missing here. priority*/effort* are optional; when present, create-issue sets them too (pipeline.issueDefaults supplies omitted values).

pipeline._comment: Optional. Every key below is shown at its default; omit any you don't need to change. `python3 sdlc_next.py show-config` prints the effective values.

locks._comment: Per-branch flock every branch-writing command takes; `{worktreesRoot}` expands to worktrees.root. SDLC_LOCK_DIR in the environment overrides `dir`.

stack._comment: Per-epic isolated runtime stack (provision-epic-stack / teardown-epic-stack). Config-only isolation: your compose must read COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME, every key under `ports`, and `dataDirKey`. Placeholders: {profile} {n} {project} {envFile} {secretsFile} {dataDir} {workspaceRoot}.

gates._comment: Global gate defaults; a profile's own `gates` override these for epics that match it.

productWip._comment: Repo-wide cap on units sitting at Stage=Product with an open Gate A (awaiting-human-review / feedback-received). next-action and list-design-ready stop starting fresh product delegations at the cap; 0 disables.

issueDefaults._comment: Priority / Effort create-issue sets when neither a flag nor an lld Task line names one.

pipeline._models_comment: Optional `models` ({"<role>": "opus|sonnet|haiku"}) and `fanout` ({"<review-role>": {"allowed", "maxChildren", "model", "axisModels"}}) override the plugin's hooks/model_policy.json per role; a hook enforces the result on every Agent call.

workItemProvider._comment: Which WorkItemProvider get_work_item_provider() returns. Only "github" is implemented -- Jira is a documented seam (README.md, "Initiative-driven lifecycle"), not built. Naming anything else is a refusal, not a silent fallback.

pipeline._classification_comment: How classify_unit tells an Initiative from an Epic from a Task; an issue matching no rule is "other", never a guess. Shown label-based; create-issue adds the kind's label itself. Either way every created issue also gets its native Issue Type, so the repo must be in an org with those types provisioned -- to classify by type instead, set a rule's "field" to "issueType" and "value" to the type's exact name. This is the ONLY way an Epic is recognised -- a standing or legacy epic needs the epic rule to match too, alongside its profile label.

profiles._comment: Ordered; the first whose `match` label is on the epic wins, `"*"` is the catch-all. A profile bundles the behaviour that used to be hardcoded to epic:standing/epic:legacy. Missing toggles inherit the shipped defaults; `gates` inherit the global `gates` above.
profiles.name: legacy

gates._comment: A standing/RTB backlog: no human gate -- the orchestrator waives both (waive-gate).
